text:
karthik: Quick follow-up after we closed the sampling RFC. I ran a small staging batch and noticed ~0.7% of traces that we intended to keep for cost-attribution end up without billing tags downstream. Not sure if it’s a race in agent samplers or a pipeline enrichment miss.

ana: ugh, can you paste an example trace id?

karthik: trace: 01F8ZB2K7... (shortened). Repro pattern: request is marked "keep" at edge, but by the time it hits trace-enricher the `billing.key` is missing.

mike: is this specific to prefix sampling or the new dynamic sampler?

karthik: dynamic sampler. I added a debug log at edge, it emits `sampling.decision=keep` and `billing.key=acct-42`. Then the request goes through the auth proxy which sets customer headers, then our ingress LB -> routing -> trace-ingest. Somewhere between LB and trace-enricher the billing header is stripped.

emily: could be the nginx sidecar config we rolled last week that rewrites headers for health checks. saw something similar with `x-client-ctx`.

ana: note: our contract currently says "instrumentation must carry `billing.key` in trace attributes if sampling decision==keep". But that contract only applies at service ingress. We might need to explicitly require it at every hop or set an immutable `trace.billing_key` in the trace proto when decision is made.

julie: I prefer copying decision+billing into the trace envelope right away so downstream cannot lose it. Minimal change: when sampler keeps, add an attribute `trace.meta.billing_key` with origin=edge. That should survive proxy header drops.

mike: agree. downside: larger traces (tiny) and possible privacy surface; but we already store billing tags elsewhere. Also need to ensure private customers are ok with billing key in ingested traces.

karthik: good point. For Private deployments we can config toggle. For hosted/dedicated we should propagate. Implementation idea: at sampler, set both HTTP header and a transient trace attribute on the in-memory span proto: `trace_attrs["redwood.billing.key"] = "acct-42"`. The trace encoder writes attrs into the first batch message so enricher can read it.

emily: sample proto snippet I played with:
```
span.resource_attrs["redwood.sampling.decision"] = "keep"
span.resource_attrs["redwood.billing.key"] = "acct-42"
```
that worked in local test.

sre-bot: deploy note: changed nginx sidecar 2026-02-14 03:12 UTC -> revert candidate if header rewrites are problematic.

ana: also want to add a sampling reason field: `redwood.sampling.reason` (cost|anomaly|debug) so billing attribution can have confidence levels.

julie: +1. For downstream pipelines, add an enrichment rule: if `redwood.billing.key` missing AND `redwood.sampling.decision==keep`, attempt to reconstruct from `x-customer-id` or fallback to `unknown` and emit metric `enrich.billing.missing`.

mike: duck-typing corner case: some partners send `x-account` not `x-customer-id`. We need a small canonicalizer step in ingest that maps legacy headers to `redwood.billing.key`.

karthik: action items: 1) Mike to add canonicalizer in ingress (PR), 2) Emily to add sampler proto attr write (PR + unit tests), 3) Julie to open small RFC addendum to require trace-level billing attr for hosted/dedicated, and 4) Ana to update SLO docs about the `enrich.billing.missing` alert we’ll create.

ana: noted, will create the alert with a soft threshold at 0.2% first.

mike: I'll also add a quick integration test simulating header rewrite by proxy.

emily: will push POC tonight and ping for review.

karthik: thanks all. If we see >0.5% after fixes we should schedule a postmortem. For now tracking in infra-obs board. :thumbsup:
